findings.what: Pac-Man (free) has no way to leave a run: no Lobby, Leave or hold-to-leave button and no key, so the only way back to the lobby is to die, while Slither has hold Q / CASH OUT and Paper has LEAVE.
findings.where: public/js/chomp/chompMain.js:463-468 backToLobby is only wired to the end card (lines 202, 451); Escape only works for a paid flow (line 531)

findings.what: In a free Slither room on a phone the leave button says "CASH OUT" (in about 7 px text) and leaving shows a "Cashed out" card, although nothing is staked; Paper's free room says "LEAVE".
findings.where: public/js/slx/slxHold.js:106-107 (label never switches for free rooms; 0.66rem at the 0.7 page scale); card verdict in public/js/slx/slxCard.js

findings.what: Paper free: you hold LEAVE ("Leaving 1.9 s, release to cancel") but the card then says "Cashed out" with "Best land", which is money wording in a free room.
findings.where: public/js/paper/mp/paperArenaMain.js:745 (verdict 'Cashed out' for free too)

findings.what: Watching Slither, the watched player is listed twice on the leaderboard: once in the list and again as the gold "you" row with a slightly different length (Mila 5,169 and Mila 5,284; Sanjay 2,428 and 2,431).
findings.where: public/js/slx/slxHud.js:178-180 (own row built from the length box with watchedName() even when that snake is already in the list)

findings.what: On a phone, Slither's empty-table Spectate bar sits off to the left and cuts its own text to "Nobody is playin...", unlike Paper and Pac-Man where it is centred and whole.
findings.where: public/js/slx/slxWatch.js:95-97 (PHONE_RIGHT 184, PHONE_SIZE 80 passed to DSWatchBar.open at line 366); plate in public/js/shared/dsWatchBar.js

findings.what: Phone leaderboards cut names of about 11+ characters ("CosmicTo...", "SockPup...", "BoldRacc...", "TinyThun..."): the name column is only 66 px wide.
findings.where: public/js/shared/dsEnd.js:259 .dsb width 128px on phones

findings.what: While spectating Slither or Paper on PC the chat still shows the "T Chat" hint, but pressing T does nothing because watchers cannot type.
findings.where: public/js/shared/dsChat.js:91 (dsc-nosend only hides the phone button, not the PC hint)

findings.what: Slither on PC never says how to leave (no "Hold Q to leave" line), while Paper shows "Hold Q to leave" bottom left.
findings.where: public/js/slx/slxHold.js:75-85 (Q works, no hint drawn) vs public/js/paper/mp/paperArenaMain.js:965

findings.what: The Pac-Man share card calls the game "Chomp" while the lobby, page title and end card call it Pac-Man.
findings.where: shared/shareGames.js:22 name: 'Chomp' (shared/chompName.js holds the real shown name)

findings.what: End cards word the same fact differently: Pac-Man says "Rank #6 of 6", Paper and Slither say "Top rank 12th".
findings.where: public/js/chomp/chompMain.js:444 facts vs paperArenaMain.js:685 and public/js/slx/slxCard.js:175

findings.what: Each game's own HUD uses its own typeface and leave button: Paper uses PT Sans Caption and a grey 72 px "LEAVE" circle bottom left, Slither uses Arial/Lucida and an amber 84 px "CASH OUT" ring bottom centre (phone only), Pac-Man uses Press Start 2P and has no leave button, while the shared board and cards are Archivo.
findings.where: public/css/paper-arena.css:5,55; public/js/slx/slxHold.js:105-131; public/chomp.html (Press Start 2P link and #title styles)

findings.what: The in-game chat uses Segoe UI on cool blue-black bubbles with a different gold caret, while the end card, Spectate bar and lobby use Archivo on warm ink.
findings.where: public/js/shared/dsChat.js:44-99 (font "Segoe UI", rgba(14,16,22), caret #f0b43c)

findings.what: The ping/FPS readout is in the system monospace (Consolas on Windows) while every other number on the site is IBM Plex Mono.
findings.where: public/js/shared/dsPerfHud.js:43

findings.what: Game overlay controls are under thumb size on phones: chat button 40x40, Hide chat 24x24, end-card Share pill 79x32, share sheet close 34x34, Spectate Lobby chip 93x42.
findings.where: dsChat.js .dsc-btn/.dsc-mute; dsEnd.js:203 .dse-share height 32px; dsShare.js .dss-x; dsWatchBar.js .dsw-lobby height 40px

findings.what: Pac-Man has no "P clip" recorder, while Slither shows the P clip dot top left and Paper shows it bottom left.
findings.where: public/chomp.html (no /js/clip/clipRec.js); server/sl/slBoot.js:94; public/paper-arena.html:59 data-dot="bl"

findings.what: The empty-table Spectate view only says "Nobody is playing yet" and never says it is the $0.50 table you picked; on Paper it is a big blank pale disc on a blue sky.
findings.where: public/js/shared/dsWatchBar.js WORDS.empty; public/js/shared/dsEmptyArena.js LOOKS.paper

findings.what: Paper's top-left land bar writes the percentage in a shade of the bar's own colour, so it is hard to read (blue on navy, purple on purple while watching).
findings.where: public/js/paper/paperRender.js:530-560 (score bar, stock paper.io drawing)

findings.what: The Coming soon pages for Agar.io and Battleship are plain Arial with an 8 px-radius 38 px gold button, unlike the lobby's Archivo and 10 px buttons, and spell the game "agar.io" where the lobby says "Agar.io".

findings.where: public/v2.html:3746-3760 (locked/soon games keep the full detail layout); public/v2.html open_() lines 5503-5520

findings.what: Typing /tanks drops you on the lobby home with no message about why.
findings.where: server/index.js:2798-2801 gamePage redirect for locked ids (shared/lockedGames.js)

findings.what: The same game is "Bowmasters" on its lobby card but "Tanks" in its page title (and /tanks in the URL).
findings.where: public/v2.html:3702 name 'Bowmasters' vs public/tanks.html <title>Tanks · DuelSeries</title>

findings.what: Battleship uses its own cool navy palette (#0d1117 background, blue-grey #a3adbb/#7c869a text) while the lobby, Tanks and the shared cards use the warm ink palette (#100e0b, #a89c8a).
findings.where: public/css/battleship.css:16-25

findings.what: On the phone game screen the main buttons are under thumb size: Play 232x42, Spectate 112x42, Back 46x41.
findings.where: public/v2.html:3115 .back, 3139 #gobtn, 3145 #specbtn (phone sizes)

styleNotes: Lobby baseline: Archivo + IBM Plex Mono, warm ink #100e0b, cream text #f5f1e8, secondary #a89c8a, bone #f4f1ea primary buttons with ink text, gold #f0a830 only for money, 10 px button radius, 18 px card radius.

Shared game UI that already matches the lobby: dsEnd card (Archivo 650 15-16 px buttons 52-54 px tall, radius 10, Plex Mono 52-62 px figure), dsWatchBar (Archivo, 999 px bone Lobby chip, 56/64 px warm-ink round buttons, 16 px plate radius), dsShare sheet.

Shared game UI that does not match: dsChat (Segoe UI 14/12.5 px, rgba(14,16,22) bubbles, caret #f0b43c, input radius 16), dsPerfHud (ui-monospace 11 px), Coming soon page (Arial 22/16/13 px, 8 px radius gold button).

Per-game HUD type: Slither Arial/Lucida (their client, canvas), Paper PT Sans Caption, Pac-Man Press Start 2P with arcade yellow #ffff00 and 6 px radius on its own menu, Battleship Archivo on navy #0d1117, Tanks Archivo on warm ink.
Leave controls: Paper grey translucent 72 px circle "LEAVE" (PT Sans 12 px) bottom left + "Hold Q to leave"; Slither phone amber 84 px ring "CASH OUT" bottom centre, PC nothing shown; Pac-Man none.

Free end cards show "Free" as the big figure (dsEnd.js:393-404, Owen's pick) with the score moved into the facts; verdicts differ per game: "You died", "Killed by X", "You crossed your own trail", "Caught by a ghost".
Inside the lobby frame /sl is drawn at 0.7 on phones, so its HUD and the shared bars are sized in a 549 px layout (Lobby chip 93x53 css = 65x37 on screen).
Reduced motion: every card and bar captured fully drawn; dsEnd plays its short entrance for everyone by design. Nothing looked half-finished.
Agar.io, Battleship and Bowmasters could not be played (Coming soon / locked), so their HUDs were not compared; their colours come from source only.
keep: One shared result card (dsEnd) on Slither, Paper and Pac-Man: same panel, same Lobby / Spectate / Play again row with the next step widest, Share pill top right, low on the phone under the thumb.

One shared Spectate bar (dsWatchBar) everywhere: bone "Lobby" chip top left, round previous/next and a name plate; Next swaps player at once (Sanjay to BoldRaccoon, Pebble to wacky_wren, River1990 to Major2013).
Empty table views that never look dead: Slither shows its hex map in the red rim, Paper its floor on the sky, Pac-Man its card art blurred.
One shared leaderboard top right in every game with your own row as a gold pill.
The ping/FPS readout sits in the same bottom-right spot in every game, coloured dot included.
Paper's hold-to-leave: ring on the LEAVE button plus "Leaving 1.9 s, release to cancel" in the middle of the screen.
Lobby round trip works: end-card Lobby and the Spectate Lobby chip both close the frame and land back on the game's screen, no reload.
Share sheet with a real preview card (score, rank, time, game art) and Copy invite link / Share.
Phone chat sits top left away from the thumbs and its input is 16 px (no page zoom on focus).
No JS errors, no sideways scroll and no overflow in any game frame on phone or PC.
Tanks' waiting card (warm ink, Archivo, spinner, "Free table. Nothing staked.") is the cleanest pre-game state and matches the lobby.
notReached: Agar.io menu, HUD, end card, chat and Spectate: Coming soon live (window.DS_SOON = agar, battleship); /ag answers the Coming soon page, the server refuses joins and watchers, and ag.html rendered from source on the live origin sends you to the lobby when not framed.
Battleship placement, match, end card and Spectate: Coming soon; only its waiting card ("Not seated") was rendered from worktree source, not reachable by a player.
Bowmasters (Tanks) in-game: locked in shared/lockedGames.js and /tanks redirects to the lobby; only its waiting card was rendered from source (the server answers nothing, so it waits forever).
dsSeatHold (seat hold): not used by any games-a game (only Rooftop Snipers, Crossy Road, Air Hockey, 8 Ball Pool) and it has no look of its own (it writes text into the host page's line).
Paper PC chat by T: a synthetic T keypress inside the frame did not open the box (the 2026-10-28 sweep confirmed a real T works); phone chat opened in all three games.
Slither PC hold-Q leave card: synthetic Q did not reach a leave before the guest died; the phone CASH OUT hold did reach the "Cashed out" card.
Paid-room HUDs, paid end cards and money states: out of bounds (no paid joins). The $0.50 tables were only watched (read only) for the empty-arena state.
Some PC chat captures (Pac-Man PC, a Paper PC motion run) show the phone chat layout because the probe's touch emulation carried over from the previous phone job; not counted as a finding.
